2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1 The brief fact of the present appeal is such that on 11.2.2023, the deceased was going with his motorcycle No.GJ-7- EH-8402 and at 7.00 pm when he reached at the place of accident, at that time, opponent No.1 being driver of Car No.GJ- 1-RS-4157 who was driving the car in rash and negligent manner dashed with the vehicle of the deceased.

As a result, the accident took place and deceased sustained severe Shakuntalaben Harshkumar Dabhi vs Vijaybhai Vasantlal Patel on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83610592/
1 injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The legal heirs of the deceased have filed aforestated claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3242/2024 ORDER DATED:
09/12/2024 undefined Vehicle Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.35,00,000/-.
The learned Tribunal vide impugned judgment and award dated 18.06.2024 has granted compensation to the tune of Rs.16,60,900/-.
Hence, the present appeal.

3. Learned advocate Mr.Hiren Modi assails the impugned judgment and award on the ground that learned Tribunal has granted compensation on lower side and submits that learned Tribunal was required to take rate of minimum wage while calculating the compensation instead of taking Rs.7500/- as monthly income of the deceased.

He would further submit that learned Tribunal was required to grant compensation under non- pecuniary heads as per the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Shethi - (2017) 16 SCC 680 which is reiterated in case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., versus Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur - (2021) 11 SCC 780.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Shethi - (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd., versus Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur - (2021) 11 SCC 780
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He would submit that learned Tribunal has committed serious error in attributing 15% negligence to the deceased in absentia of any evidence on record and therefore he submits that finding of learned Tribunal to the extent of attributing 15% negligence to the deceased is incorrect and requires to be set aside.
4.
On the other hand, learned advocate Mr.Saksena appearing for the respondent - Insurance Company supports the impugned judgment and award and submits to pass necessary orders.

5. Having heard learned advocates for both sides and perused the impugned judgment and award as well as record and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3242/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/12/2024 undefined proceedings of the case, it could be noticed that accident took place between two vehicles where one of them was driven by deceased himself and it dashed with the another vehicle being Car bearing No.GJ-1-RS-4157 driven by the opponent at night hours.

In para 8 of the impugned judgment and award, learned Tribunal has assessed the issue of negligence as under :
"8.
That the Applicant has filed her examination-in- chief in form of Affidavit vide Exh. 19, and stated as averred in the claim petition.
Thereafter, claimant has been cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for Opponent No. 2, wherein, claimant has stated that she has not seen the accident.

It is further stated that at the time of accident,
deceased had held driving licence.
This Tribunal has considered the complaint at Exh. 23; Panchnama at Exh. 24 as well as the deposition of Applicant.
It is not in dispute that the accident had taken place on 11-02- 2023, at 7:00 p.m., between Motorcycle and Car.

This Tribunal has also considered the FSL Report at Exh 33,
looking to the same, it appears that the present accident has occurred due to contributory negligence of driver of offending vehicle as well as the deceased.

It is also required to be noted herein that as the road was 15 Feet wide, moreover,
offending vehicle was also bigger in size, the driver of offending vehicle ought to have taken more care and caution while driving on the road.
At the same time, deceased should have taken care and caution while driving on the road at night, but he had failed to do so.

Hence, considering the evidence on the case file, it clearly appears that the present accident occurred due to contributory negligence of driver of the Shakuntalaben Harshkumar Dabhi vs Vijaybhai Vasantlal Patel on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83610592/
2 offending vehicle i.e. Car bearing Registration No. GJ 01 R. S. 4157 as well as the deceased, himself.

sentences.text: Thus, from the aforesaid discussions, this Tribunal is of the considered view that the present accident has occurred due to 85% negligence of the driver of offending vehicle as well as 15% negligence of the deceased.
Thus, as per the above discussion, my answer to the issue No. 1, is, in partly Affirmative."
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3242/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/12/2024 undefined 6.
On perusal of the above reasons stated by the learned Tribunal, it could be noticed that the learned Tribunal while attributing 15% negligence to the deceased did not give any reason.
Only because the deceased was driver of one of the offending vehicle, he has been marked with responsibility of causing the road accident to the extent of 15%.
The driver of the other offending vehicle did not enter into the witness-box and even he has not contested the claim petition despite being served.

The Insurance Company who has obtained order under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 to contest the claim petition on all the grounds available to the driver and owner did not do anything to secure the presence of the driver before the learned Tribunal and further to secure the best evidence of the road accident.
The principle of res ipsa loquitor would be applied in the present case as none of the eye-witness of the road accident has entered into the witness box.
The spot panchnama produced at Exhibit-24 recorded the position of the errant vehicle post accident.
The deceased was riding Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle at the relevant time.
His vehicle was kept on east edge of the road.
The driver side bumper and front mud guard etc. have received damage.
The car has received damage on the front side.
The blood stains were found in the circle of 5 feet.
The allegations of causing road accident is made against the driver of car, FIR of which is produced at Exhibit-23.

So looking to these aspects and more particularly when driver of the offending vehicle did not step into the witness box to rebut the evidence on record, it is a fit case to take the adverse inference against the driver of the car.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3242/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/12/2024 undefined 7.

At this juncture, I may refer to the judgment of this Court in case of United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Yakum Alibhai Molvi and others, being First Appeal No.2355 of 2006, wherein in para 8 and 9, it is held as under :
"8.

sentences.text: Regard
being had to the rival submissions of learned advocates appearing for the respective parties, it is an admitting position that driver of the fiat car died in the road accident.

The driver of the luxury car who is the best person and having specialized knowledge of all the relevant facts of road accident in question and is duty bound to explain the accident did not enter into the witness box.

In the present case, neither written statement was filed by luxury bus driver to contend that the averments made by the claimants are not true; nor the driver of the luxury bus was examined to deny such averments.
In this circumstance, the principle of "res ipsa loquitur" would be attracted.

(See 1976 (1) SCC 793 The Krishna Bus Services Ltd., vs Smt. Mangli & Ors.)
9.

3 permit the tribunal to draw adverse inference against him.

In Iswar Bhai C. Patel & Bachu Bhai Patel vs Harihar Behera & Anr [1999 (3) SCC 457], the Supreme Court has held in paragraph 17 as under:
"17.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Admittedly defendant No.1 had an account in the Central Bank of India Limited,
Sambalpur Branch which his father, namely, respondent No.2, was authorised to operate.
It is also an admitted fact that it was from this account that the amount was advanced to the appellant by respondent No.2.

It has been given out in the statement of respondent No.2 that when the appellant had approached him for a loan of Rs.7,000/-, he had explicitly told him that he had no money to lend whereupon the appellant had himself suggested to advance the loan from the account of respondent No.1 and it was on his suggestion that the respondent No.2 issued the cheque to the appellant which the appellant, admittedly, encashed.

This fact has not been controverted by the appellant who did not enter the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3242/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/12/2024 undefined witness box to make a statement on oath denying the statement of defendant (respondent) No.2 that it was at his instance that respondent No.2 had advanced the amount of Rs. 7,000/- to the appellant by issuing a cheque on the account of defendant (respondent) No.1.

Having not entered into the witness box and having not presented himself for cross-examination, an adverse presumption has to be drawn against him on the basis of principles contained in illustration (g) of Section 114 of the Evidence Act."
8.
As far as calculation of the just and fair compensation is concerned, what is needed to see is that fatal accident took place on 11.02.2023 where deceased has lost his life.

According to claim petition,
he was serving as Conductor in Tankers mainly employed with Amul Dairy and his age was around 23 years.

The rate of minimum wage for unskilled labourer on the day of accident is Rs.9445/-;
semi-skilled labourer is 9653/- and skilled labourer is 9887/-.

Taking up clue from that, I adopt Rs.10,000/- per month as income of the deceased in absence of any permanent source of income while taking up the age of deceased as less than 30 at the relevant time and 40% would be added towards compensation for future prospects.
Claimant No.1 is widow, claimant Nos.2 and 3 are minor children and claimant Nos.4 and 5 are parents.
Thus, looking to the number of claimants, 1/4 deduction from income of deceased towards pocket and personal expenses is to be made.
The multiplier of 18 would be applied as per the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Pranay Sethi (supra).
The compensation under non- pecuniary heads are also required to be rationalized.
For all the above purpose, this Court has taken assistance from judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Pranay Sethi (supra) and Satinder Kaur (supra).

Therefore,

 Particulars Amount  Future dependency Loss 2  =Rs.10,000/- + 4000/- (40% rise)
 =Rs.14,000/- minus 1/4 personal exp.
 =Rs.10,500/- x 12 months x 18 multiplier  Loss of Estate   Funeral Expenses  Shakuntalaben Harshkumar Dabhi vs Vijaybhai Vasantlal Patel on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83610592/
4  Consortium (Rs.48,400/- x 5 claimants) 
 Total 2  Less: Amount already awarded by Tribunal 1  Additional amount which is awarded  9.

Therefore, I hold that the claimants are entitled to get the enhanced compensation of Rs.8,85,400/- with 7.5% p.a. interest from the date of filing the claim petition till its realization,
which would meet the ends of justice.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.
10. For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
10.1 The present appeal is partly allowed.
10.2 The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced amount with interest as stated herein above within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3242/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/12/2024 undefined 10.3

The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimants, by account payee cheque / NEFT / RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
10.4 While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the courts fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
10.5 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
